name: create_sql_migration_split_column
description: Migrates full_name into first/last columns via a table rebuild
prompts: schema.sql creates and seeds contacts(id, full_name, email) where full_name is always 'First Last' (exactly one space). Write migration.sql that restructures the table to contacts(id, first_name, last_name, email) - splitting every existing full_name at the first space - with NO full_name column remaining and all ids/emails preserved. SQLite's ALTER TABLE can't drop/split columns, so use the standard rebuild recipe: CREATE a new table, INSERT ... SELECT with substr/instr to split, DROP the old table, ALTER ... RENAME. Plain SQL, runs via executescript.

test_setup_files.test_migration.py:
import sqlite3

conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
conn.executescript(open('schema.sql').read())
conn.executescript(open('migration.sql').read())

cols = [r[1] for r in conn.execute('PRAGMA table_info(contacts)').fetchall()]
assert 'first_name' in cols and 'last_name' in cols, f'columns: {cols}'
assert 'full_name' not in cols, f'full_name must be gone: {cols}'

rows = conn.execute(
    'SELECT id, first_name, last_name, email FROM contacts ORDER BY id').fetchall()
assert rows == [
    (1, 'Ada', 'Lovelace', 'ada@calc.io'),
    (2, 'Grace', 'Hopper', 'grace@navy.mil'),
    (3, 'Linus', 'Torvalds', 'linus@kernel.org'),
], f'data must survive the split with ids preserved: {rows}'
print('PASS')
